Seniors | Representative Andrea Salinas Skip to main content 403 Cannon House Office Building, Washington, DC 20515 Email Me (202) 225-5643 Seniors Congress must do more to strengthen the financial and physical well-being for older Americans. I have been a champion for benefits and programs that older Americans rely on, and I strongly oppose any effort to undermine Social Security or Medicare. That’s why I cosponsored the Social Security Fairness Act that repeals provisions of law that reduce or eliminate benefits for some Americans who have devoted their careers to public service. Medicare must also be modernized to ensure its success for future generations. I support proposals to close loopholes that allow the wealthiest Americans to avoid paying their fair share in taxes, which will keep Medicare funded for decades into the future. Modernizing these programs will lead to significant improvements for older Americans. I am committed to protecting and bolstering these programs to ensure everyone can enjoy a healthy and financially secure retirement. Veterans | Representative Andrea Salinas Skip to main content 403 Cannon House Office Building, Washington, DC 20515 Email Me (202) 225-5643 Veterans As the daughter of a Vietnam veteran, I am committed to fulfilling our nation’s promise to the Americans who put their lives on the line to defend our country. We owe it to them and their families to deliver the care and benefits they’ve earned and deserve. Congress must ensure veterans’ basic needs are met, and we must improve access to and the quality of VA health care, including mental health care. That’s why I support efforts to expand access for veterans to the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP), as well as proposals to expand dental care through the VA to all veterans. Further, we must ensure veterans have access to education and training opportunities as they transition into the civilian workforce to ensure they are positioned for success in emerging and competitive fields. Upholding our promise to our veterans also means caring for their families, especially families who have lost a loved one in the line of duty. I support raising the amount of VA benefits that are paid to surviving family members of servicemembers and veterans, as well as reducing the time period families have to wait to receive these benefits. As a co-chair of the Bipartisan Mental Health Caucus, I recognize the immense and unique mental health struggles veterans face when returning to civilian life. I have consistently sought to elevate commonsense legislative solutions that will provide veterans with the help they need as they navigate these challenges. If you’re a veteran who needs help with a federal agency, please reach out to my office HERE , and my team will be more than happy to assist you. More on Veterans Image Reps. Education | Representative Andrea Salinas Skip to main content 403 Cannon House Office Building, Washington, DC 20515 Email Me (202) 225-5643 Education As a mom, I understand the importance of a strong public education system. From cradle to career, I am committed to supporting policies that make sure our education system works for everyone. I strongly support providing federal funding for school districts throughout the country to provide curriculum that teaches critical thinking and important life skills. Congress must also do more to support our educators. Teachers should not be struggling to pay their bills due to inadequate salaries – they should be rewarded for choosing an educational career pathway by having access to student loan forgiveness. Our education system must prepare students for the economy of the future. I have championed legislation that would improve access to educational pathways in the Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM) fields. I also recognize that attending a traditional four year college or university is not the right fit for everyone, nor is it necessary to have a successful career and meaningful work. I support increasing federal investments in career and technical education (CTE), as well as improving access to community colleges. Students need skills when they enter the workforce, and alternative higher education pathways can provide them. No matter what education path our students choose, it must be affordable and free from crushing student loan debt. Congress should increase funding for student financial aid and allow for more flexible uses for college savings plans. There’s more work to do, and ensuring that all students have access to affordable and flexible post-secondary education options – and a strong, effective public education system to prepare them – should be among our nation’s top priorities. Agriculture | Representative Andrea Salinas Skip to main content 403 Cannon House Office Building, Washington, DC 20515 Email Me (202) 225-5643 Agriculture Oregon’s Sixth District is home to a variety of specialty-crop growers that produce everything from blueberries to wine grapes to hazelnuts. The farming tradition in the Willamette Valley dates back hundreds of years. Due to the region’s unique and favorable climate conditions, it was publicized in the 1820s as a “promised land of flowing milk and honey.” As your representative, one of my foremost priorities is to help secure and strengthen the district’s farming tradition. That is why I am pleased to be a member of the House Committee on Agriculture , particularly as Democrats on the Committee work to mitigate the harm caused by the drastic cuts to the Nutrition Program, and consider the next Farm Bill. The Farm Bill is a legislative package passed once roughly every five years that impacts the food and agricultural products grown and developed in the United States; sets forth the federal support that farmers across the country rely on;  and provides food under the federal nutrition programs. The last Farm Bill Reauthorization was in 2018. Unfortunately, my Republican colleagues have broken from a decades-long tradition of bipartisan cooperation on the Farm Bill by pulling out pieces of the Farm Bill and including them in their partisan reconciliation package – the One Big, Ugly Bill. One of these pieces was the nation’s largest federal nutrition program, the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP). The One Big, Ugly Bill included almost $200 billion in cuts to SNAP, which 740,000 (1 in 6) Oregonians rely on — causing families to go hungry. The Republicans delivered on President Trump’s tax cuts for billionaires, at the expense of children, veterans, and seniors who need to eat. I strongly opposed these cuts, and I will work to undo the harm they will cause. Health Care | Representative Andrea Salinas Skip to main content 403 Cannon House Office Building, Washington, DC 20515 Email Me (202) 225-5643 Health Care Health care is a human right, and I’m fighting to ensure all Americans can access the quality, affordable care they need and deserve. I’m committed to bringing down costs for those who need it most, especially working families and seniors. Millions of Americans depend on Medicare and Medicaid (in Oregon, we know this as the Oregon Health Plan) for care, and we need to protect – not undermine or defund – these programs. I support proposals to expand Medicare to cover dental, hearing,  vision, and mental health care, as well as proposals that allow for drug price negotiations that would reduce the price of life-saving medication. I also understand that health care can only be as good as it is available. In particular, our rural communities have little to no access to quality, comprehensive care. I am committed to finding solutions to these care shortages, including legislation that would strengthen Community Health Centers and provide incentives for medical professionals to work in shortage areas. Our private health care system is too complex, burdensome, and expensive. I will continue working to improve and expand federal programs like Medicare and Medicaid while also reconsidering the nature of a profit-driven private health care industry that prioritizes profits over patients. Americans deserve the highest quality health care our country can provide, and I will continue working to move us closer to that goal.   More on Health Care Image Rep. Immigration | Representative Andrea Salinas Skip to main content 403 Cannon House Office Building, Washington, DC 20515 Email Me (202) 225-5643 Immigration Image As the daughter of a Mexican immigrant, I know that we must be a nation that welcomes immigrants and those seeking refuge. Immigrants in Oregon and around the country are a part of the fabric of our communities and work in critical jobs that help keep our society running. Without their contributions, the United States would not be nearly as strong as it is today. That said, it’s clear our immigration system is broken and in desperate need of modernization. We must do so in a way that prioritizes safety and humanity for all, including in border communities who are reeling from an unsustainable surge in crossings. I support legislation that would provide for comprehensive immigration reform by creating an earned pathway to citizenship, investing in smart border security improvements, and addressing the root causes of migration by fostering political stability and creating conditions for economic development opportunities in Central and South America. These changes would bring much-needed stability to our immigration system. For too long, many immigrants in this country have lived under a constantly changing set of rules. This is particularly true for Dreamers, individuals who came to the United States as children and were provided temporary protection from deportation under the Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals (DACA) program. I am committed to finding a long-term solution and pathway to citizenship for Dreamers, as well as for those who have been working and contributing to our economy. I remain steadfast in my commitment to stabilize our immigration system and ensure our borders are safe, secure, and efficient. More on Immigration Image Rep. Civil Rights | Representative Andrea Salinas Skip to main content 403 Cannon House Office Building, Washington, DC 20515 Email Me (202) 225-5643 Civil Rights Throughout our country’s history, civil rights leaders have fought to make the United States better for everyone. From the battle to end segregation to the fight for marriage equality, we’ve made tremendous progress in the last several decades. As a member of the Democratic Women’s Caucus’ executive steering committee, I’m working to protect and expand gender equality across the United States. I also support legislation that empowers women by ending the gender pay gap, prohibits states from punishing women for interstate travel to access reproductive health care, protects access to birth control, and guarantees paid parental leave.   I’m also proud to serve as a leader in the Congressional Hispanic Caucus (CHC). Oregon’s Sixth District is home to a thriving Latino community, and, as a member of CHC leadership, I’m championing my community’s needs in Washington, D.C. I’ve introduced legislation like the Mental Health for Latinos Act and the Disaster Relief for Farmworkers Act . As a Latina, I know the importance of solidarity between people of all races, and I value collaborating with my colleagues in the Congressional Black Caucus and the Congressional Asian Pacific American Caucus to address the myriad challenges facing communities of color in America. In addition to my caucus leadership roles, I’m a member of the Congressional Equality Caucus (CEC), which advocates for the fair treatment of LGBTQ2SIA+ individuals in America. I will always stand up for the civil rights of every American, no matter their race, religion, gender, or background.    More on Civil Rights Image Rep.
